prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Preparing desktop graphics and pet rendering layers..."]
1: ["Desktop Pet Controls", "Control your pet easily from the system tray menu anytime.", "Got It"]
2: ["Setting up desktop integration. Look for your pet icon in the system tray when ready."]
3: ["Account Sync Safeguard", "Your pet choices are linked to your sign-in account and will restore automatically when you re-login.", "Continue"]
4: ["If photo processing encounters issues, default pet options will automatically be available."]
5: ["First Interactive Steps", "Learn how to click, move, and call your pet on your desktop display.", "Start Tutorial"]
6: ["Verifying Display Setup", "Checking system permissions to ensure your pet displays smoothly over desktop windows.", "Launch Pet"]
7: ["Signing in connects your desktop pet to your cloud account so progress is never lost."]
8: ["Choose Your Pet Creation Path", "Pick an instant starter pet or create a unique custom companion from your own photos."]
9: ["Your pet certificate is ready! Review details below before introducing your companion to the desktop."]
